transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-29 15:00 PDT | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM); Janelle Ortiz (Head of ML), Marcus Li (CTO), Priya Shah (Infra), Andre Gomez (Finance)

Summary: Quick QBR-style checkin focused on governance (audit logs, SSO, model rollouts), cost momentum as usage grows, and a proposed pilot for reserved capacity. Customer is seeing spike from holiday promos; wants cost predictability and guardrails for rollout.

Topics: governance & compliance; reserved vs hosted economics; autoscale burst behavior; cache/KV impact on cost; model rollouts and canary policies; next-step benchmarks and pricing.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Sofia: All right thanks everyone for joining, appreciate you carving out the time. quick agenda — governance, costs as you scale into holiday, and then a short pilot proposal. sound good?
00:10 Janelle: Yup that works. we had a pretty big uptick in chat volume last week with the promo and, uh, some tail latencies started showing.
00:18 Marcus: yeah from infra side we saw token spend jump 4x, so finance is looking at predictable commitments.
00:24 Andre: hi all, from finance, we need a clear way to project spend and what reserved vs hosted does to our unit economics.
00:30 Sofia: Understood — we'll walk through committed capacity options and a variant of burst/overprovisioning. Ethan, do you want to pull up the numbers on reserved vs pay-as-you-go?
00:36 Ethan: yep, quick caveat — these are illustrative: for your modal profile (median prompt 1.2k tokens, avg response 220 tokens) dedicated reserved capacity gives about 30-45% unit cost savings versus hosted on same model family when fully utilized. but the key is utilization — if you can't keep utilization above ~60% the break even shifts.
01:00 Priya: hmm that 60% threshold — in our case traffic is very spiky, more like 10-15% most days and big surges during promos. we need burst without overpaying.
01:12 Ethan: there are two knobs — reserved pools + autoscale with burst buckets, or keep hosted and lean on prefix caching/kv. For spiky traffic a small reserved baseline plus burst to hosted often hits the sweet spot. though that introduces routing complexity.
01:30 Marcus: routing complexity = more ops for us. also curious about data residency and audit logs for the hosted fallback. Andre: are there compliance concerns?
01:40 Andre: finance less, but risk/compliance wants full audit trails for customer prompts for regulatory reasons.
01:46 Sofia: we can provide audit logs and exportable event streams for hosted requests; for Private deployments you get more granular control and on-prem options. question — is the audit log retention requirement strict (e.g., 7 years) or short term?
01:58 Janelle: It's 18 months for our particular vertical. plus SSO enforced and role-based access.
02:05 Maya: quick note — Redwood's RBAC + SAML SSO integration supports session audits and token-level cost attribution; we can map to your internal roles.
02:14 Priya: and KMS? if we use hosted fallback we still need envelope encryption with our KMS.
02:20 Ethan: yes we support customer-managed KMS for private and dedicated deployments; hosted can integrate with your cloud KMS through a connector — there are some extra compliance steps but it's supported.
02:31 Janelle: good. on the cost side, what about caching — we have a lot of repeat prompts and product descriptions. how much can caching reduce spend?
02:39 Ethan: depends on repeat ratio. for prefix/KV caching, if you can get ~20-30% hit rate you'll see ~15-25% token cost reduction because you avoid recomputing the prefix and reduce decode tokens. for reranks/embeddings it's even higher if you cache embeddings for unchanged documents.
03:00 Marcus: does caching complicate privacy/audit? we need to ensure cached values don't persist beyond retention.
03:05 Sofia: we can scope cache TTLs and tie them to retention policies; plus we can enable encrypted caches that are rotated by your KMS.
03:13 Priya: ok. what about model rollouts — we need canary, automatic fallback, and quality regression alerts.
03:19 Ethan: Redwood supports staged rollouts with canary traffic, A/B, and automatic fallback to a compatible variant. We also integrate evals so you can tie regressions to prompt sets and trigger alerts when quality drops.
03:36 Janelle: perfect, that'll be useful. now — the big ask: Andre wants a clear three-month cost projection under two scenarios: 1) keep hosted with optimization levers, 2) small reserved baseline with burst to hosted.
03:50 Andre: yes, and show expected worst-case spend during 99th percentile promo days.
03:56 Ethan: we can run a simulation using your traffic trace. need the past 90 days of token-level traces and a few representative prompt families.
04:05 Priya: we'll export logs but need to obfuscate PII first — is that okay for benchmarking?
04:10 Sofia: absolutely, obfuscated traces work fine for model-agnostic throughput/cost sims. we'll provide a safe ingestion method.
04:16 Janelle: Related question: how does quantization impact latency/quality? are there recommended quant profiles for our workload?
04:23 Ethan: quantization reduces memory and often improves throughput; for many transformer families int8/q4 formats give ~1.5-2x throughput improvement with slight quality tradeoffs. we can run small A/B evals on your prompt set to measure acceptance.
04:40 Marcus: speed numbers — what's the median token latency improvement we can expect?
04:44 Ethan: ballpark, for generation heavy workloads, 20-40% per-token latency improvement depending on model and sequence length. but again must verify on your exact prompts.
04:55 Andre: okay, that helps. also — if we go reserved, how flexible are rollups? like mid-quarter upsizing?
05:02 Sofia: reserved capacity contracts can include scaling addenda — a baseline commit and options to add incremental capacity with pro-rated billing. we can sketch a flexible addendum in the pricing sheet.
05:12 Andre: fine. finance will want to see 'what happens if utilization drops' — is there a cooling-off clause?
05:18 Sofia: yes we can include a one-time rightsize within the first 90 days for new deals; specifics depend on term length. we'll outline options in the spreadsheet.
05:26 Janelle: any recommended guardrails on model family deprecation? we had an incident where a vendor deprecated an older model and the subtleties in responses changed.
05:34 Ethan: we recommend pinning model versions for canaries and performing pre-deploy evals. Redwood Optimize can recommend compatible model variants and run regression alerts when outputs shift beyond thresholds.
05:47 Maya: i'll flag that we should set up a recurring eval run weekly on the core prompt set.
05:52 Priya: ok, ops question — network egress for hosted fallback. we have strict VPC egress rules. will Redwood route through our VPC?
05:59 Ethan: yes, with Private you get a customer-controlled egress path; for dedicated we can peer or use a private link; for hosted fallback we offer a VPC connector option. there are some setup steps but it's supported.
06:13 Marcus: noted. any competitor notes to be aware of? we evaluated Anthropic's private offering and AWS Bedrock for native cloud integrations.
06:21 Sofia: Anthropic had good safety tooling but less flexible dedicated capacity; Bedrock integrates with AWS ecosystem nicely, but our differentiation is the unified runtime and cost tooling across hosted/dedicated/private.
06:33 Janelle: sounds good. next — pilot scope proposal?
06:36 Sofia: propose a 6-week pilot: 2 weeks benchmarking with obfuscated traces, 3 weeks reserved baseline + burst policy test in staging, and 1 week QA and rollback rehearsal. success criteria: median latency under 150ms for 90% of chat tokens, and cost per 1M tokens within X% of projected numbers.
06:52 Marcus: timeline ok, we need staging parity first.
06:56 Ethan: we'll provide a benchmark harness and a starter config for autoscale + cache.
07:02 Priya: small ask — can we test KMS envelope flow in staging without exposing keys?
07:07 Ethan: yes, we have a test mode that simulates KMS calls; for full integration we'd do customer KMS onboarding later in pilot.
07:16 Andre: finance will also want a 'what-if' run for worst-case promo day — could Redwood run a stress sim?
07:22 Sofia: yes, Ethan will simulate 10k concurrent chats with mixed-size prompts; we'll attach the modeled spend projection.
07:29 Ethan: quick note — we need 3 canonical prompt families and your 90-day token trace anonymized.
07:36 Janelle: we'll deliver that by Monday.
07:38 Sofia: perfect, so to recap action items and owners — Ethan runs benchmark and stress sim, Sofia shares pricing and contract sketch, Priya shares VPC/KMS details, Janelle shares prompt sets and traces. anything else?
07:52 Maya: I'll set up the pilot Jira board and invite the stakeholders.
07:56 Andre: please make sure finance sees the reserves addendum and the cooling-off clause.
08:01 Sofia: will do. any final questions?
08:05 Marcus: none from me.
08:08 Janelle: all good. thanks.
08:11 Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pricing sheet and benchmark plan — expect emails and calendar invites. bye.

Recap (auto): 58-minute checkin focusing on governance, reserve vs hosted economics, caching and quantization opportunities, pilot plan, required artifacts for benchmark.

End of transcript.
